concerns.text: The plan (and spec) define a column as “faithful” when the corrected p‑value ≥ 0.05 **and** the effect‑size is below a threshold. Using a non‑significant p‑value as evidence of similarity is methodologically unsound because failure to reject the null does not confirm equivalence; low power or small sample size can produce non‑significant results even when distributions differ. This undermines the validity of the fidelity classification and the downstream success criteria (SC‑002).
